name: Linnea Olson

died.text: Linnea Olson died on 15 November 2021, at the age of 61. A tribute posted on her blog on 3 December 2021 says she died at home, and that her adult children and family members were with her.
died.quote: Evalynn Linnea Olson, known to all as “Linnea”, died at the age of 61 on Monday, November 15, 2021.
died.quote2: She was able to pass away at home, her adult children and family members were with her.
died.label: a tribute on her blog, 3 December 2021

also.label: ALK Positive tribute
also.note: This page also gives the date as 15 November 2021.

summary: Linnea Olson wrote for years about living with ALK-positive lung cancer. This page records what she and her family published.
It is not evidence that a treatment works, and it is not a claim that she was cured.
She wrote that she was diagnosed with stage IB non-small cell lung cancer in 2005.
She switched her care to Thomas J. Lynch, Jr, MD, and wrote that she was sure that decision saved her life.
After surgery and chemotherapy, the cancer was later classed as stage IV. By 2008, she was told she had three to five months to live.
In October 2008, she became the fourth person with this cancer to take experimental crizotinib.
She later took ceritinib, then lorlatinib.
The tribute on her blog said she had lived with lung cancer for 17 years. That is a fact about her life, not a claim that a drug cured her.

quotes.text: Eleven years after being diagnosed with stage 4 lung cancer, my focus is no longer on a cure but rather on living a high-quality life with my disease.
quotes.label: The ASCO Post, 25 August 2016, by Linnea Olson, as told to Jo Cavallo

quotes.text: When I was finally diagnosed with stage IB NSCLC in 2005, the tumor was confined to my lower left lobe and was 5 cm.
quotes.label: The ASCO Post, 25 August 2016

quotes.text: I’m sure the decision saved my life.
quotes.label: The ASCO Post, 25 August 2016, about switching her care to Thomas J. Lynch, Jr, MD

quotes.text: In October 2008, I became the fourth person in the world with NSCLC to take the then-experimental drug crizotinib (Xalkori).
quotes.label: The ASCO Post, 25 August 2016

quotes.text: Although the drug has given me 2 years of disease stability, there are now signs of cancer progression.
quotes.label: The ASCO Post, 25 August 2016, about lorlatinib

timeline.decision: She was diagnosed with stage IB non-small cell lung cancer. She switched her care to Thomas J. Lynch, Jr, MD, at Massachusetts General. She had surgery to remove the lower lobe of her left lung, then chemotherapy.
timeline.label: The ASCO Post, 25 August 2016

timeline.decision: The cancer was reclassified as stage IV. She wrote that she was told she had three to five months to live. A biopsy showed she was ALK-positive.
timeline.label: The ASCO Post, 25 August 2016

timeline.decision: She became the fourth person with this cancer to take experimental crizotinib. She later wrote that it gave her three years of high-quality life before she became resistant to it.
timeline.label: The ASCO Post, 25 August 2016

timeline.date: after crizotinib (exact start date not given in the 2016 essay)
timeline.decision: She joined a phase I study of another ALK drug, ceritinib. She wrote that it bought her enough time to enter a trial of lorlatinib.
timeline.label: The ASCO Post, 25 August 2016

timeline.decision: She still took lorlatinib. She wrote that it had given her two years of disease stability, and that there were then signs of cancer progression. She named her oncologist at that time.
timeline.label: The ASCO Post, 25 August 2016

timeline.decision: She died at home, at the age of 61, with her adult children and family members with her, according to the tribute on her blog.
timeline.label: a tribute on her blog, 3 December 2021

status.quote: Evalynn Linnea Olson, known to all as “Linnea”, died at the age of 61 on Monday, November 15, 2021.
status.note: Her last first-person treatment update that we opened is the 25 August 2016 ASCO Post essay, when she still took lorlatinib and there were signs of progression. A 6 April 2022 American Lung Association page is dated after her death, so this page does not treat it as a living update.

actions.what: Early lung cancer (stage IB): a 5 cm tumour in the lower part of her left lung
actions.quote: When I was finally diagnosed with stage IB NSCLC in 2005, the tumor was confined to my lower left lobe and was 5 cm.

label_basis.quote: surgery to remove the lower lobe of my left lung

actions.what: Switched her care to Thomas J. Lynch, Jr, MD
actions.quote: After a bad experience with the oncologist who had diagnosed me, I switched my care to Thomas J. Lynch, Jr, MD (now CEO and Chairman of Massachusetts General Physicians Organization). I’m sure the decision saved my life.
actions.date_note: Her 2016 essay tells this after her 2005 diagnosis and gives no separate date.

milestone.quote: I switched my care to Thomas J. Lynch, Jr, MD (now CEO and Chairman of Massachusetts General Physicians Organization). I’m sure the decision saved my life.

actions.what: Surgery removed the lower lobe of her left lung, then four rounds of chemotherapy
actions.quote: After undergoing surgery to remove the lower lobe of my left lung, I was prescribed four rounds of a combination regimen of docetaxel and cisplatin chemotherapy to kill any errant malignant cells and potentially cure my disease.
actions.date_note: Her 2016 essay tells this after her 2005 diagnosis and gives no separate date.

actions.what: Tumours in both lungs; now stage IV
actions.quote: I was unresponsive to the chemotherapy, and within months, tumors began invading both lungs, and my cancer was reclassified to stage IV.

actions.what: Told she had 3 to 5 months to live
actions.quote: By 2008, with few other treatment options to deploy and the cancer rapidly advancing, I was told I had 3 to 5 months to live.

actions.what: She and her son started counselling; she said goodbye to relatives
actions.quote: To prepare both my young son, just 11 at the time, and myself for my impending death, we started counseling, and I made a cross-country trip to say my goodbyes to relatives.
date_basis: By 2008, with few other treatment options to deploy and the cancer rapidly advancing, I was told I had 3 to 5 months to live.

phases.title: The first ALK drug trial
phases.span_note: Her 2016 essay: crizotinib from October 2008 gave her 3 years before resistance.

actions.what: Fourth person in the world with this cancer to take crizotinib, then experimental
actions.quote: In October 2008, I became the fourth person in the world with NSCLC to take the then-experimental drug crizotinib (Xalkori).

milestone.quote: In October 2008, I became the fourth person in the world with NSCLC to take the then-experimental drug crizotinib (Xalkori).

actions.what: High-quality life on the drug, then resistance
actions.quote: instead it gave me 3 years of high-quality life before I became resistant to it and the chance to enroll in a phase I study investigating another ALK inhibitor ceritinib (Zykadia).

phases.title: More ALK drug trials
phases.span_note: Her 2016 essay gives no start date for ceritinib.

actions.what: An early trial of ceritinib, which bought her time
actions.quote: Although I didn’t get as long a delay from disease progression with ceritinib as I did with crizotinib, it bought me enough time to enter a phase I trial for the next-generation ALK/ROS1 tyrosine kinase inhibitor lorlatinib
actions.date_note: After resistance to crizotinib, as told in her 2016 essay.

actions.quote: Although I didn’t get as long a delay from disease progression with ceritinib as I did with crizotinib, it bought me enough time to enter a phase I trial for the next-generation ALK/ROS1 tyrosine kinase inhibitor lorlatinib
actions.date_note: After ceritinib, as told in her 2016 essay.

actions.what: Two years stable on lorlatinib; now signs of progression
actions.quote: which I still take today. Although the drug has given me 2 years of disease stability, there are now signs of cancer progression.

actions.what: She wrote that she advocates for patients’ rights and research funding
actions.quote: I’ve become a staunch advocate for patients’ rights and work to increase funding for cancer research, and the work is rewarding.

milestone.quote: I’ve become a staunch advocate for patients’ rights and work to increase funding for cancer research

actions.what: She wrote that she had gone back to chemotherapy and joined two more early trials
actions.quote: In the years hence, I have returned to chemotherapy, but also enrolled in two more phase I clinical trials.

actions.what: She died at home, aged 61, with her family
actions.quote: Evalynn Linnea Olson, known to all as “Linnea”, died at the age of 61 on Monday, November 15, 2021.

label_basis.quote: She was able to pass away at home, her adult children and family members were with her

phase_links.cause: A gene test of a tumour found an ALK change, and she joined the first trial of a drug aimed at it. She wrote: “Just in the nick of time medical science intervened.”

sources.quote: A biopsy of one of my tumors used for genetic sequencing revealed I was positive for the fusion oncogene anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK).

Just in the nick of time medical science intervened, as I was found to have a newly identified driver in lung cancer, an ALK (anaplastic lymphoma kinase) mutation. On October 1, 2008, I became the fourth person in the world with NSCLC to enroll in a first-in-human trial targeting ALK.

phase_links.cause: After 3 years she became resistant to crizotinib. She wrote that the drug also gave her “the chance to enroll in a phase I study” of another ALK drug.

sources.quote: instead it gave me 3 years of high-quality life before I became resistant to it and the chance to enroll in a phase I study investigating another ALK inhibitor ceritinib (Zykadia).
